full_judgment:
2. Rule was issued to show cause as to why the impugned order issued by the respondent No.3 vide Letter No. 06.39 dated 02-10-2003 cancelling the order of appointment/promotion of the petitioner to the post of Marketing Manager (Current Charge) vide Officer Order dated 15-4-2003, evidenced by Annexure-B to the writ petition, and why the order dated 4-10-2003 passed by the respondent No. 4 demoting the petitioner in the lower position of Manager, Technical and Special Project (MT & SP), evidenced by Annexure-F to the writ petition, should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 4. Dr M Zahir, the learned Advocate, appearing for the writ petitioner, has taken us through the writ petition and submitted that, the writ petitioner was appointed as an officer in the post of Terminal Supervisor in the then Pakistan National Oils Company Ltd, now Jumuna Oil Company Ltd, a subsidiary of Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation, in Grade-Ill on 19-11-1968 and that subsequently, through promotion he was posted as Manager, Technical and Special Project (MT & SP) and that while he was holding the said post as MT & SP he was placed in a higher post in Special Manager grade as Marketing Manager (Current Charge) by office order dated 15-4-2003 issued by the Corporation, subject to regularisation through usual process of Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation and Jumuna Oil Company Ltd, and that the writ petitioner has the requisite qualification for promotion to the said post of Marketing Manager, which post the petitioner was holding on Current Charge basis, and that the petitioner was given initially Current Charge of Marketing Manager, subject to regularisation according to the long exercised practice for promotion followed by Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation, the highest Authority of the Subsidiary Company, in consultation with the concerned General Manager of Jumuna Oil Company Ltd and that in case of promotion to the post of Marketing Manager and General Manager (Chief Executive) of the company, initially current charge is given and subsequently, the said promotion is regularised/ confirmed in due course by the Corporation. That while the writ petitioner was discharging his duties as Marketing Manager (Current Charge) to the satisfaction of the company, the respondent No.3 by its letter dated 2-10-2003 (Annexure E) addressed to the respondent No. 4 cancelling the earlier office order dated 15-4-2003 (Annexure-B) issued by the respondent No. 3 appointing the petitioner in the post of Marketing Manager (Current Charge) and the said letter dated 2-10-2003 was issued without showing any reason or any cause whatsoever and that the same was in violation of the Service Rules of the Company, which do not provide any provision for demoting an officer without following the course of law, and that the respondent No. 4 thereafter issued an order, communicated by letter dated 4-10-2003 (Annexure F), advising the petitioner to join in the lower post of MT & SP (M-1) and for that matter to report to the Marketing Manager and being aggrieved against such order of demotion the writ petitioner has moved this Court and obtained the Rule. 

 5. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate that the letter dated 2-10-2003 has been issued by the Secretary of the Corporation to the General Manager of the Jumuna Oil Company Ltd who is not authorised to do, and that the writ petitioner is an officer of the Jumuna Oil Company Ltd and, as such, any order regarding his service has to be made by the said Jumuna Oil Company Ltd and not by the Corporation and that the General Manager of the Company has no authority to make any recommendation for filling up the post of the Marketing Manager, which as per law, has to be done by the Board of Directors of Jamuna Oil Company Ltd. The learned Advocate stressed on the point, that the impugned order of reversion has. been made without jurisdiction by the Corporation and that the General Manager cannot pass the order dated 4-10-03, evidenced by Annexure- F to the writ petition, asking the writ petitioner to join the office of MT & SP and to report to the Marketing Manager. The learned Advocate tried to impress upon us that the writ petitioner is a fit candidate for promotion and, in fact, it is the practice of the Jumuna Oil Company Ltd to place an officer in the next higher post on current charge basis before regularising him in the said higher post on promotion with the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the company subject to approval by the Corporation. 

 On a plain reading of the said Annexure-E it appears that the appointment in the post of Marketing Manager (Current Charge) given by the letter dated 15-4-2003, evidenced by Annexure-B to the writ petition, which is an office order, has been cancelled and the charge of the Marketing Manager was given to the General Manager of the Jumuna Oil Company Ltd as additional charge and further it was requested that in order to fill up the vacant post of Marketing Manager as per rule and practice a proposal should be placed with the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Company before the Corporation and that the said letter (Annexure-E) has been endorsed to the Company Secretary of Jumuna Oil Company Ltd, Chittagong to take necessary steps on its part. 

 8. Annexure-F at page 51 of the writ petition, is the letter dated 4-10-03 by which the writ petitioner has been reverted back to his original post of MT & SP and was asked to report to the Marketing Manager and the said letter has been issued by the General Manager of Jumuna Oil Company Ltd. 

 9. According to Rule 25(3) of the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation Rules, 1976, the General Manager is the Chief Executive of the Subsidiary Company like Jumuna Oil Company Ltd, and that as per Article 13 of the Articles of Association of Jumuna Oil Company Ltd the General Manager of the Company shall be appointed by the Corporation i.e. Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation. 

 10. Annexure-B at page 32 of the writ petition is the letter dated 15-4-2003, containing the office order by which the writ petitioner was given the charge of Marketing Manager (Current Charge) and the said office order was issued by the Secretary of the Corporation and copy of the same has been sent to the Company Secretary of the Jumuna Oil Ltd, Chittagong. The order is subject to "until further orders". 

 12. The learned Advocate appearing for the writ petitioner, in reply, submitted that the General Manager of the Jumuna Oil Company Ltd should not be instrumental in making the proposal for filling up the vacant post of Marketing Manager, the appointment of which is subject to the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Company, alleging that the relationship between the writ petitioner and the General Manager is not on good terms. We are unable to appreciate this submission inasmuch as in Annexure-E it has been categorically mentioned as under: 

 Thus it appears that the impugned (Annexure- E) letter has been issued, as per order, addressing the General Manager, who is the Chief Executive of Jumuna Oil Company Ltd, and the said letter has been endorsed to the Company Secretary of the Jumuna Oil Company Ltd for taking necessary steps for placement of the proposal for appointment of Marketing Manager before the Board of Directors of the Company for required recommendation. Therefore, it is the General Manager who is to make the proposal for placing before the Board of Directors of the Company through the Company Secretary and it is the function of the General Manager, being the Chief Executive of the Company to make such proposal for filling up vacant posts in the Company and thus there is no illegality in the order. The order contained in Annexure- F, the letter dated 4-10-2003, asking the writ petitioner to report to the Marketing Manager on his reversion cannot be said to be an illegal order or an office order without jurisdiction.
